newsitem.title: UK: UK analyst sees Ivorian cocoa crop at 990,000 T.
newsitem.headline: UK analyst sees Ivorian cocoa crop at 990,000 T.

text.p: Ivory Coast's cocoa output should reach a total of 990,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season (October/September), according to a UK-based independent commodities research company.
A cocoa analyst said the the estimate for the main crop was between 850,000 and 900,000 tonnes.
"Last year was exceptional in terms of the size and the quality of the mid crop," said the analyst who did not want to be named.
He added that the long-term trend of the country's production was upwards but the trees looked tired after the record yield of an estimated 1.2 million tonnes in 1995/96.
"You have a certain amount of exhaustion," he said.
Changeable weather conditions complicated crop forecasts this year but recent rains after a dry spell were likely to benefit the tail end of the main crop and the mid crop, the UK analyst said.
The forecast near the top end of the wide range of estimates that have emerged from various analysts in the last month.

Another UK analyst Robert Fish said last week the total Ivorian crop would be at least one million tonnes after improved weather conditions. His company, PCR Ltd, had pegged the crop at 1.065 million tonnes earlier this month.
Ivorian officials meanwhile have insisted that the crop would not exceed 950,000 tonnes. One diplomat said last week the crop was likely to be between 850,000 and 900,000 tonnes.
The U.S. General Cocoa has forecast the crop at between 850,000 and 900,000 tonnes in its latest weekly newsletter.
